> 天道運而無所積，故萬物成；帝道運而無所積，故天下歸；聖道運而無所積，故海內服。

The way of heaven turns and accumulates nothing, and so the ten thousand things come to be.

The same clause repeats three times: 無所積. Whatever this chapter is about, it is about that.

## 積: to stockpile, to settle into a shape

積 is to pile up, to hold, to come to rest in one place and stay.

Turn and do not 積: not stopping anywhere, not hardening into a fixed form.

Then the sentence that follows the repetition is the real argument: whatever 積s becomes a thing that can be taken. This is the same anxiety as 胠篋's 利器 — a sharp instrument of the world, which someone will seize. Two chapters, one diagnosis: make it into an object, and it acquires an owner.

## 靜 is not cultivated

聖人之靜也，非曰靜也善，故靜也 — the sage's stillness is not because stillness is good and therefore practiced.

Then the reason: 萬物無足以鐃心者. 鐃 reads 撓 — to stir, to rake. Nothing is able to rake the heart; therefore still.

Stillness here is a result, not a discipline. Which knocks out most of what is sold as calm: if you are producing the stillness, something is still raking.

## 水靜則明燭鬚眉

Still water reflects beard and brow; 平中準, and the master carpenter takes it as his standard.

The image is not decorative. It says clarity comes from not moving, and that the standard is taken from what has settled — not from what is being pushed.

## 天樂, defined by four negatives

天樂 is not human pleasure. The text defines it by what it does not do: 不為戾, 不為仁, 不為壽, 不為巧.

Not cruel, not beneficent, not long-lived, not skillful — each refused as a thing to be credited to one's own account. That is the whole content: joy with no itemized receipt.

## 落 means to net

知雖落天地 — 落 reads 絡: to net, to wrap, to cover.

Knowledge can net heaven and earth and still not move a thought of its own to worry about it. The capacity is total; the accounting is zero.

## 糟魄: dregs

魄 reads 粕 — the residue after brewing, the husk after hulling. 輪扁 uses it for written words, and the edge is uncomfortable: not that writing is bad, but that writing is the part that was left after the extraction.

He is saying this to a ruler while making a wheel, and his claim is narrower than "books are useless": the thing that cannot be transmitted is the 分寸, the exact measure at the point of contact.

## 得心應手

得之於手而應於心 — it comes through the hand and answers the heart.

The idiom it became is weaker than the original. The original is not about fluency. It is about a layer of measure that has no words, which is why the chapter puts it in a wheelwright's mouth rather than a scholar's.

## The test

Name one thing you have made into a form — a method, a brand, a doctrine, a persona. Then ask the 積 question: has it settled into a shape someone could pick up and use without you? If yes, you have built something. The chapter's question is whether it was worth building.
